verdicts.reason: Quotes verify verbatim, but the tree converges. `unmarketable` is reserved throughout for ONE trigger — unanswered provenance: 20.01.04:52 ('Artist cannot answer the provenance question | Import completes and records land in an unmarketable tier'), 20.01.04:67 States row ('Import succeeded, provenance unanswered | Records exist, marked unmarketable'), D-03 at 20.01.04:93, and 20.01-fan-graph-owned-audience-cx.md:40 ('If the provenance assertion is missing ... records land in an unmarketable tier'). Answered-provenance imports are throttled-but-sendable everywhere the machinery is actually wired: 20.01.02:114 (DT-03) 'weak-provenance records are throttled/tiered rather than trusted', 20.01.02:93 'artist-asserted, deliverability-downgraded tier', 20.01.02:129 'provenance strength and consent staleness drive send throttling and tiering', 20.01.04:83 'import provenance is the input to warm-up throttling', 20.03.03:88 'a fresh import forces a warm-up ramp', 20.03.04:94 'imports set the warm-up tier', and fanbase-direct-to-fan-cx.md:76 trigger chain '... provenance ... resolve at dispatch -> throttle tier -> send'. The single '(unmarketable-until-re-permissioned)' gloss at 20.01.02:88 sits in a User-Sees cell of an edge-case row about a fraudulent provenance claim; it is not a Decision, and the same table contradicts it at :93. D-08 (20.01.02:147), the only normative statement about artist-asserted, sets provenance assignment and says nothing about marketability. The residual calibration question is tracked: 20.01.04 Q-02 ('What are the warm-up tiers and thresholds') -> /create-prd-architecture, and Q-01 (re-permission lawfulness) -> /create-prd-security.

CONFIRMED against the files. 20.03.03:61, :93 and D-08 at :107 make a per-fan frequency cap a mandatory dispatch gate ('this node checks the cap at dispatch and defers/suppresses over-limit fans') and assign the policy to 20.02. A grep for 'frequency cap|frequency capping|fatigue|send budget' across the whole domain returns hits ONLY in 20.03.03 (:61, :81, :93, :107) and 20.01.03:61 — zero hits in 20.02-segmentation-superfan-intelligence-index.md, 20.02-segmentation-superfan-intelligence-cx.md, 20.02.01-segment-builder.md, 20.02.02-superfan-score.md or 20.02.03-perk-entitlements-presale-eligibility.md. The named handoff target does not exist either: 20.03.03:93 cites a '`-cx.md` frequency-fatigue thread', but 20.03-broadcast-fan-messaging-cx.md contains only CX-01..CX-05 (composer/routing/deliverability/scheduling) plus R-01/R-02 — no fatigue thread. 20.02's open questions (index Q-01..Q-03 at :60-62; cx Q-01..Q-02 at :126-127) track score explainability, fixed-vs-tunable scoring, cross-entity segments, the CX-04 consent/entitlement question and the CX-03 ratchet — none tracks a frequency cap. DT-04 at 20.03.03:81 explicitly rules out 20.01.03's fan-set tiers as the same object ('a fleet-wide ceiling, artist-blind' vs 'a per-fan, per-artist budget'), and 20.01.03:49-50 gives the default 'All' tier no cap at all, so the only existing cap cannot serve the gate. Period, value, setter, scope and defer-vs-drop must all be invented, with nothing tracking the gap. Blocking: the dispatch gate is normatively required and cannot be built.

The stale text is real (20.03.02:40-44 and DT-02 at :85), but it is explicitly superseded inside the same file. 20.03.02:119 Q-04: 'RESOLVED — yes ... meta/constraints.md § Project Surfaces now declares Mobile (PWA) in v1 ... Ratified as ideation-index D-28 ... So push is not lost: it arrives in v1 as PWA web push, with a native surface in phase 2 for exactly this domain.' 20.06.02:124 Q-01 does the same for the fan side. Verified against source: meta/constraints.md:293 Mobile (PWA) row reads 'v1: web is installable as a PWA (home-screen, web push for gig alerts ...)' and :294 Mobile (native) 'Phase 2'. The two 20.05 restatements are not stale at all — they assert only that the channel 'cannot reliably deliver on iOS', which is exactly the caveat Q-04 carries forward verbatim ('iOS Safari web push requires the fan to install the PWA to the home screen', constraints.md ⚠️ VERIFY, D-70) and which 20.06.02:124 repeats ('its iOS objection survives as constraints.md's recorded ⚠️ VERIFY item'). No planner reading 20.03.02's own Open Questions table drops push from v1.

CONFIRMED. 20.01.01:80 reads 'Partial data — record exists but every resolved key is unverified (all guest/import) | Record renders; marketing send is hard-disabled at the record level until a stronger key verifies' — 'import' is named explicitly, and the key ranking at 20.01.01:36-37 puts 'asserted email from import' below 'verified email (platform-witnessed a confirmed click)', so an import-only record has exactly one unverified key. 20.01.04:45-46 then creates 4,335 such records and states 'the new records enter a warm-up tier — first sends are throttled'. This is a second, independent axis from #001: 20.01.02's provenance machinery grades consent strength, never identity verification, so nothing in the consent tier ladder resolves it. The gate is also inconsistent inside 20.01.01 itself — the States table at :95 gives the same population 'reduced contactability', not zero, while :67 reserves the absolute form ('contactable = false, marketable = false') for the genuinely emailless Hide-My-Email case. No marker anywhere: 20.01.01's Q-01..Q-04 (:134-137) cover marketplace observations, cross-entity isolation, DSAR reach and retention — none this. Downgraded from the finding's framing to warning because 20.01.01:56 delegates contactability 'governed entirely by 20.01.02' and :117 'resolution never widens contactability', which a careful implementer may read as making :80 subordinate — but the text as written is an unreconciled record-level hard block on the domain's entire import product.

Quotes verify, but the finding conflates two taxonomies on different axes and at different layers. The consent-ledger purpose (marketing/transactional/service, 20.01.02:23, :39, DT-04:115) is a property of the (fan, entity, channel, purpose) grant in the ledger; the campaign purpose-type (transactional/general/release/live-event-geo, 20.01.03:57) is a marketing sub-taxonomy used to match frequency TIERS ('Shows near me' admits live-event-geo, 'New releases' admits release) — 20.01.03:58-62 resolves transactional as one branch and the other three collectively as 'marketing', so the campaign enum spans exactly two of the three ledger purposes by construction, not by omission. The ledger itself is explicitly not domain-owned: fanbase-direct-to-fan-cx.md:376 routes 'DSAR, erasure, portability, the consent ledger' to CX-M18, keeping only marketing consent domain-owned, and 20.01.02 DT-01 (:112) says 'CX-M18 is the general ledger ... this feature consumes it'. Service/operational messaging is likewise routed out: 20.03.02 DT-04 (:87) and D-06 (:110) place 'an urgent operational change ... tied to a purchase/relationship' in CX-M07's transport, not in broadcast, so the finding's own worked example ('your membership renews Friday') has a stated home. DT-04's rule that a marketing grant does not license a service message is a constraint on the shared ledger, not a requirement that domain 20 ship a service campaign type. What remains is enum membership in the ledger schema — spec-layer detail.

The map-row and §2 quotes exist, but CX-14's own detail section says the opposite of what is claimed. fanbase-direct-to-fan-cx.md:342-343: 'The keep-vs-lose policy is owned by 20.05 (its open Q-01: does a lapsed member keep what they downloaded?)'; :354 heads the synthesis 'Medium confidence — pending 20.05.02 Q-01 resolution'; :359 'the keep-vs-lose policy (whether previously downloaded copies survive) is the unresolved 20.05.02 Q-01 that must be answered before this edge is fully specifiable'; and the map row itself (:25) ends 'keep-vs-lose call shared with 20.05.02 Q-01'. The 'fail-closed to locked on ambiguity' at :356 is scoped by its own sentence to the atomicity race — 'the library never shows a stale unlocked state after a lapse' — and :350 states the opposite of a blanket lock ('owned purchases never lock'). CX-14 therefore governs the lifecycle-event race and explicitly disclaims the retroactivity policy. The deferral is well-formed at both ends: 20.05.02:126 Q-01 '[OWNER] Do lapsed members keep what was released while they paid? | User | /create-prd' and 20.06.03:192 Q-04 '[OWNER] ... aligned with 20.05.02 Q-01 ... One decision, taken there, settles both files'. The interim default is stated identically in all three files (20.05.02:73, 20.05.01:78, 20.06.03:120).

Quotes verify, but 'survives everything' is glossed by its own enumeration and restated in scoped form by the file the finding says contradicts it. 20.04.03:154 D-01's Context lists exclusively seller-side events — 'Physical fails, artist delists, pressing cancelled' — and its rationale in 20.06.03:176 D-03 is 'Entitlements survive delisting, artist departure, and campaign failure. The fan paid us. Their ownership cannot be contingent on someone else's later decision.' A refund/chargeback is the buyer un-paying, not someone else's decision; the antecedent fails. 20.06.03 is the only file in the tree that addresses the refund->entitlement question at all (:128), and the same file states the survival rule in the deliberately scoped D-03 form rather than as 'everything' — so it is internally consistent, not in conflict with itself. Every 20.04.03 case that D-01 actually governs is a seller-side one (:96 removal from sale, :97 takedown, :94 cancelled pressing), and 20.04.04:113-114 specifies the money side of refund/chargeback in detail without ever asserting the entitlement stands. No competent implementer builds 'any chargeback yields a free permanent album' from a decision row whose examples are all delisting.

Both quotes verify, but ownership is explicit and undisputed, and the divergent wording is the non-owner's loose house term. 20.04.03 uses 'settlement' as its generic word for payment completion throughout, not as the acquirer settlement leg: :103 'Entitlement is granted at payment settlement', :101 stock 'decremented atomically at payment settlement', :104 'Either the charge settled ... or it did not', :83 'At payment settlement: digital entitlement granted'. The same row the finding cites defers the rule: 20.04.03:108 ends 'Sales before the change pay the old plan, after pay the new (20.04.04)', and the Cross-Cut Note at :136 states '20.04.04 applies it'. 20.04.04, which owns the payout engine, is precise and repeated — :82 'the payout plan version live at payment authorization (D-01, 20.04.01 D-02)', :99, :115, :120, :121, D-11 at :178 ('plan version at payment authorization'), and Q-08 at :191 which carries the version-resolution work forward on the same term. The parent decision 20.04.01:192 D-02 is deliberately moment-agnostic ('the plan version at sale time governs each sale'), so it does not corroborate 'settlement'. An implementer builds the payout binding from 20.04.04.

Both quotes verify, but 'blocked' in this tree consistently means a forced choice at the gate, not a refusal. 20.02.03:54's What-Happens cell says only 'Must be caught at grant time, not at on-sale'; the two exits appear in the User-Sees copy, which is the unblock path. D-03 blocks the over-PROMISE — granting 1,203 fans an implied guarantee against 300 tickets — and declaring the presale first-come removes the over-promise rather than proceeding with it, because the fans are told before they act. DT-02:76's demand that the check be 'blunt rather than a warning nobody reads' is satisfied by an interstitial that will not clear without an explicit choice, which is exactly the pattern the domain uses elsewhere for the same shape: 20.05.01:76 tier deletion 'Grandfather, migrate, or refund — a decision, never a silent drop | Forced choice at deletion'; 20.05.02:74 'deletion forces a decision ... rather than leaving dangling references'; 20.04.04:108 'a blocking interstitial fires before the product can go live' with two named options. Implementer A's reading (grant refusable only by narrowing below allocation) would make a legitimate first-come presale unbuildable, which the edge-case row expressly permits — so it is not a competent reading, it is a misreading the text forecloses.

The two quotes verify but govern different objects. 20.04.01:38-45 defines FIVE product kinds and separates `physical-record` from `merch-pod`/`merch-stocked` as distinct rows with distinct payout-plan sources, and the table's own note at :47-50 pre-empts exactly this conflation: 'The last column is the source of the split percentages, and it varies by kind ... The column was renamed from "Payout basis" so the two cannot be confused into one field.' The Detail-owned-by and Payout-plan-source columns are separate axes, so 20.04.02 owning a pressing's variant/stock detail says nothing about its split source. 20.04.02 D-01 is scoped to 'Merch splits', and its stated rationale is unambiguous about which objects it means: 20.04.02:21 'the drummer on the record has no claim on a t-shirt'. The reconciling fact is stated absolutely in the very line the finding cites — 20.04-direct-to-fan-storefront-cx.md:113 'Merch has no rights record in domain 09 — there is nothing to reference' — and again at 20.04.04:118 'Merch has no domain 09 rights record to reference'. A vinyl pressing of the artist's own recording manifestly does have one; that is the platform's founding thesis (20.04.04:95-102). The finding's failure scenario requires an implementer to classify a `physical-record` as a `merch-*` kind against an explicit six-row taxonomy.

CONFIRMED verbatim. 20.06.02-gig-alerts-near-me.md:127 and :128 are two consecutive rows of one Open Questions table both labelled 'Q-04' — :127 '[OWNER] Per DQ-04.07 / D-06 — is the alert radius the same setting as 20.01.03's? | User | /create-prd' and :128 '✅ Resolved Step 5 → D-07. One aggregate, event-keyed alert ... | Agent | Resolved'. The collision propagates into the Decisions table exactly as claimed: :116 D-06 'See Q-04' points at the radius row while :117 D-07 'Resolves Q-04' points at the aggregate row. Nothing in the file, 20.06-fan-experience-discovery-index.md or 20.06-fan-experience-discovery-cx.md flags or reconciles the duplicate. Held at warning rather than blocking: the harm the finding projects is partly mitigated because D-06's own Context column at :116 restates the live question in full ('this needs an explicit owner ruling on whether alert radius and the 20.01.03 radius are one setting or two'), so the [OWNER] item is recoverable from the Decisions table even if id-keyed collection drops it. The defect itself — one identifier bound to two rows, cited both ways — is real, objective and untracked.

CONFIRMED. 20.02.01-segment-builder.md:44 reads '| **Membership** | tier / joined-since date / active vs lapsed (no activity in N days) | 20.04 |'. The cited domain does not own any of it: 20.04-direct-to-fan-storefront-index.md's children are the catalog, merch/POD, digital sales and revenue split, and 20.04.01:45 delegates even its `members-item` kind's detail out to 20.02.03 rather than defining a membership. The real owner is 20.05.01-membership-tiers-benefits.md — :28 'a ladder of tiers, each granting entitlements', with lapse/downgrade/dunning lifecycle at :77-80 and the reverse dependency stated at :113 'Feeds [20.02.02 Superfan Score] — tenure and active tier are strong signals'. The mis-citation is isolated, not a shorthand convention: the adjacent rows in the same table cite '19 Ticketing' (:43), 'CX-M13' (:45) and '20.02.02, 20.03' (:46) correctly. 20.02.01's Cross-Cut Notes (from :101) never reference 20.05 either, so the pointer is not corrected downstream in the file. Warning rather than blocking — an implementer who follows the pointer and finds nothing will search and land on 20.05.01 — but the source column is the table's authority surface and it is wrong and unmarked.
